I checked every file that uses `Logger`. **49 files** would fail to type-check. Each one imports `Logger` by name, either from `@nestjs/common` or from `packages/common/services`. Both routes stop working:

- **Direct imports (3 files).** `load-package.util.ts`, `file-type.validator.ts` and `configurable-module.builder.ts` import `Logger` straight from `logger.service.js`. They would get "has no exported member 'Logger'".
- **Through the barrels (46 files).** `packages/common/services/index.ts` uses `export * from './logger.service.js'`, and `@nestjs/common` points to `packages/common/index.ts`, which re-exports that barrel. Once `Logger` isn't exported, neither barrel exposes it. So `streamable-file.ts` (which imports `../services/index.js`) and the 45 files importing it from `@nestjs/common` would all fail.
- **Type-only import.** `packages/core/repl/repl-function.ts` uses `import type { Logger }`, which still fails when the name isn't exported.

These files would not fail:
- `packages/common/services/logger.service.ts`: the class is still declared there, so its own uses of `Logger` still work.
- The two barrel files: `export *` doesn't report an error when a name disappears.
- `packages/microservices/external/kafka.interface.ts`: it declares its own `Logger` type.
- `nest-application-context-options.interface.ts`: it only mentions `Logger` in a comment.

I didn't find any namespace-style access (`x.Logger`) or named re-export (`export { Logger } from ...`) in the files in scope.

48 files would fail to type-check. Each one imports `Logger` by name, and there are three ways that import reaches `logger.service.ts`:

- **Direct import.** `packages/common/utils/load-package.util.ts`, `packages/common/module-utils/configurable-module.builder.ts` and `packages/common/pipes/file/file-type.validator.ts` import `../services/logger.service.js` directly.
- **Through the services barrel.** `packages/common/file-stream/streamable-file.ts` imports from `../services/index.js`, which does `export * from './logger.service'`.
- **Through the package entry point.** All the others import from `@nestjs/common`. `tsconfig.rie.json` maps that to `packages/common/index.ts`, which re-exports the services barrel. Once the export is gone, `@nestjs/common` no longer provides `Logger`.

The `export *` barrels don't fail themselves; a star re-export just stops including the name. `logger.service.ts` itself still compiles, because the class can use its own name inside the file. `packages/core/repl/repl-function.ts` fails too, even though it uses `import type`, since the name still has to be exported. `packages/microservices/external/kafka.interface.ts` also uses a `Logger`, but it's a different type from Kafka, so it's unaffected.

I found 40 files that would fail to type-check. Each one imports `isNil` by name, and would get "Module has no exported member 'isNil'" (TS2305). I found them by searching the source rather than running the compiler.

**How they reach it:**
- **12 files in `packages/common`** import it directly from `../utils/shared.utils.js` or `../../utils/shared.utils.js`.
- **28 files in other packages** import it from `@nestjs/common/internal`. In `tsconfig.rie.json`, that path points to `packages/common/internal.ts`, which re-exports everything with `export * from './utils/shared.utils.js'`. Once `isNil` isn't exported, the re-export no longer includes it, so these imports break too.

**What's not affected:**
- `shared.utils.ts` itself still type-checks, because its own uses of `isNil` refer to the declaration, which stays.
- No other barrel file (`index.ts` or similar) re-exports `shared.utils`.
- Spec files are outside the scope, so they aren't listed.

`validation.pipe.ts` is on the list even though it declares a local variable also named `isNil` inside one method. Its import still fails, and the method at line 236 calls the imported function.

If `isNil` is no longer exported, 44 files would fail to type-check. Each one names `isNil` in an import, and that import can no longer resolve:

- **Direct importers:** 13 files in `packages/common` import it from `../utils/shared.utils.js` or `../../utils/shared.utils.js`.
- **Importers via `@nestjs/common/internal`:** 31 files in the other packages import it from there. `packages/common/internal.ts` only passes the name along through `export * from './utils/shared.utils.js'`, so once the export is gone, `isNil` disappears from `internal` too.

Four files are not affected:
- `packages/common/utils/shared.utils.ts` only uses `isNil` locally, and the declaration stays.
- `packages/common/internal.ts` uses `export *`, which doesn't fail when a name is missing.
- `packages/common/index.ts` doesn't re-export `shared.utils`.
- `packages/common/pipes/validation.pipe.ts` has a local variable also called `isNil` (line 152). It still fails anyway because of its import on line 21, so it is on the list.
